pagerduty-bot: PAGER: service=inference-usw pool=dedicated-gpu severity=SEV2 — multiple nodes flapping (NotReady) in inferpool-usw, recent 5 events in 3m. runbook: /runbooks/kube-node-flap. paging: alex-m.

alex-m: on it, grabbing logs and handoff incoming.

alex-m: first quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inferpool-usw -o wide` shows 3/9 NotReady, LastTransitionTime ~ 30-120s ago.

observability-bot: metrics: kube_node_status_condition{condition=\"Ready\"} spike from 2% to 35% not-ready across the pool. node-exporter shows CPU steady, kubelet restart count increased. Linking charts: https://telemetry.redwood/inferpool/usw/reeval

sam: any signs of OOM or driver errors? last time we saw NVRM Xid.

alex-m: checking `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` on node infer-usw-3: shows repeated `kubelet: Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start sandbox container` and `dockerd: containerd: containerd: failed to start shim: exit status 1`.

alex-m: also pulled dmesg from same host, snippet: ```
[ 1234.56789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 0, GPU error: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.56800] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

leo: sounds like GPU driver/kernel panic surface. If nvidia-smi is hanging that's consistent. We saw similar in eu-west when driver upgrade + kernel combo misbehaved.

infra-bot: autoscaler: detected unhealthy nodes in ASG inferpool-usw-a, requested replacements 3 -> launching new instances (ami=gpu-2025-09-12).

alex-m: plan: cordon the unstable nodes, drain evicting inference pods to fallback pool, and push routing rule to steer traffic away from inferpool-usw for model-heavy endpoints. starting cordon on infer-usw-2/3/7.

sam: +1. For routing, I'll apply temporary policy to route 100% of traffic for /v1/generate to infer-us-east as fallback. Minimal cfg: 
```bash
curl -X POST \"https://edge-control.internal/routing/update\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_TOKEN\" -d '{\"route\":\"/v1/generate\",\"target\":\"infer-us-east\",\"percent\":100}'
```

jia: please annotate the change in the runbook and mention which customers will be affected. cust-support, any live tickets?

cust-support: Ticketstream: #INC-7712 flagged by health checks — saw 500/503 spikes and ~4x latency for a subset of requests starting 07:11 UTC. A and B customers reported degraded responses, we opened support cases. We'll preemptively notify them that we're steering traffic to fallback infra.

alex-m: cords/drains in progress. command: `kubectl drain infer-usw-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=10m`

alex-m: drain output: Evicted 18 inference pods, 2 pods failed to terminate within deadline — force-deleted. Some jobs retried on fallback.

leo: if nodes keep flapping, we should consider marking AMI/driver as suspect and pause rolling updates. Also check kernel version drift between healthy and failing nodes.

infra-bot: new nodes reported `InstanceStatus: initialising`, kubelet joined after 40s on new nodes. ASG replaced 3 nodes.

observability-bot: traffic shift executed, error rate on /v1/generate in us-west decreased from 7.2% -> 0.8% over 2m, overall platform latency returned near baseline. Linking: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/1747609123/ratios

sam: rolling note — we saw `oom_kill` on a few pods prior to GPU Xid errors; likely cascading resource pressure plus driver fault. Need to capture kubelet logs before node reboots.

alex-m: grabbed kubelet journal tail for one failed node and uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1747609123/kubelet-infer-usw-3.log

jia: customer comms: drafting message to support affected customers with ETA and mitigation steps. cc: legal for regulated customers.

leo: mitigation complete for now, but we should leave nodes cordoned until AMI/driver verification. Setting tag `investigate:gpu-driver` on replaced instances.

incident-bot: Incident 1747609123 marked MITIGATED at 07:23 UTC. Postmortem owner assigned: alex-m.

alex-m: summary: cause — GPU driver/kernel combo triggered Xid 79 on a subset of nodes causing kubelet/container runtime instability -> pods evicted/failed -> NotReady cascade. Mitigation — cordon+drain failing nodes, route traffic to fallback region, ASG replaced nodes. Next: collect crash dumps, compare AMI/driver versions, block image rollout if correlated.

sam: +1 on postmortem. I'll pull recent AMI/driver rollout history and link.

cust-support: updating tickets and sending out customer notes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
